@⁨Oscar⁩ is QJ a bust candidate?!

Dear Jailyard GMs,
I got married this year. As many of you know, that experience can lead one to reflect upon what really matters in life.
At this point, I think only Brent, Ben, Pat and Oscar are left from the inaugural year as we’ve continued to trim the fat and refine the ownership stakes…
We’ve developed an extraordinary league after 12 or 13 years. I want to let you all know, from the bottom of my heart, that the amount of time I spend reading, creating and responding to the ongoing chatter in this group, and to be associated with you all as fellow general managers is truly one of the greatest disgraces of my life.
With that off my chest, here’s this week’s power rankings. Numbers represent your projected final standings at the end of this regular season. Read em and weep.
#1 Legion of Bouz - After this team pulled the rug out from under the Judge last year and stole a championship, they continue to take the league by storm. With the best RB room around, steady young receivers and Mahomes running the ship, the chance of a repeat is good.
#2 Herb Stomp - With Eckler back and Etienne peaking like he’s three hours into an acid trip, this team has the second best RB room in the league, arguably the best if Achance can get healthy. The question is whether this team's young WRs can take the next step and their old receivers can find the fountain of youth to carry them to a ship. Nonetheless, he also holds the surefire #1 pick for next year. After disclosing the dumpster fire he built in his other league, we’re unfortunately all subject to the lessons he learned there. The long term future for this squad is good.
#3 Boonist Monks - We all recognize the irony of this loud mouths team name. His trade button is as active as his yapper. Unfortunately, this team is walking the walk too. They boast the best pass catching lineup in the league with the #1 TE and #1 WR and Kamara/Montgomery looks like a solid blockbuster if they can stay healthy. He’s enjoyed the fewest points against but it’s hard to argue that this team is a pretender. Barring injuries, this team is playoff bound. I truly regret having to say all this. Nate/Matt. This is all your fault. Luckily, he’s mortgaged his future and his stars are aging. If he doesn’t get one this year, the fall to the bottom could be swift for this squad.
#4 General Ken-Obi - This squad has top 4 points against and still 30+ points more. Unfortunately on a weekly basis it’s not working out. Too bad he didn’t get that vote passed on beating the median score or whatever that boring bullshit was…. That said, he’s got a solid lineup of freshman-junior players who could all ascend to a next level at any point. With a pretty easy schedule the rest of the way (barring his matchups with Bouz and Judge Jeudy) here’s my sleeper playoff #4 spot pick. He also loves a reverse jinx, I hear….
#5 Judge Jeudy - Undoubtedly the highlight of this team is the administration. Boasting the most savvy and handsome GM in the league, the outlook is bright. After shipping their inaugural overall #1 pick for a basket of goods, this team may have pulled off the trade of the year. If Taylor gets back to form, I might regret it. With Kyren Williams out for multiple weeks, this team is very reliant on Diggs and Hurts to carry the load. If Jacobs, Evans and some other mid tier guys can step back into stardom mode, this team could be playoff bound. But, my prediction is #5 looking in from the outside.
#6 Noble FT - This team has a scary stable of young backs that looks dangerous and should be formidable for years to come. Unfortunately there’s just not enough talent across the board at the WR or QB position to see this team ending up higher than 6. Keep building.
#7 Ghastly Greyskull Gang - This team screams #6. A bunch of guys that have ~#15 potential at their respective positions. With 910 points against, Oscar is the town bicycle of this league. Bold prediction: this team continues to get bent over on a weekly basis and is left with a middle of the pack draft pick.
#8 Father Time - This team has a solid receiver room. RB’s aren’t great. This team could make a run, but do they want to? As a bottom 4 team in the league with two top 10 WRs over 30. Can you say TRADE BAIT? If not, I think they can push for 8th place.
#9 Harlow - Injuries have plagued this team's hopes of doing anything significant. At this point, there’s way too much riding on guys who Kenny Pickett throws to for this team to truly be in the playoff hunt.
#10 BROMBTIME - I just looked at his team and nobody other than Russel Wilson is even projected to surpass double digits. His stable of RBs is like his shit talking, getting quieter and more irrelevant every week.
#11 Kittler on the Roof - This team made some big moves in the draft and early season, finding the Puka in the Rough and orchestrating a blockbuster deal for the once All-Pro caliber Jonathan Taylor. Nonetheless it’s been a volatile and disappointing first half for this squad with Calvin Ridley looking like a poor mans Christian Kirk since week 1, Najee nearing retirement at age 24 and Aaron Rodgers leaving both Garret Wilson and Ben wondering what could have been. I’d say it’s time for this team to throw in the towel and try to get as high a draft position as they can….
#12 Chudders - The other 11 of us are all really bummed we didn’t agree upon a brutal Sacko punishment for this season. Theoretically he has players on this team, but nobody remembers who. Also having traded away his first pick for someone forgettable, the forecast looks bleak for the foreseeable future for Chudders.
Nice work, Zach! A great addition to the last dozen years of glorious disgraces 😂

quote_block.text:
Behold your Jinx Power Rankings!
 
As will become customary, I offer two things at the outset of this evening power ranking: (1) a curse and (2) a boon.  First, a curse upon BRO or whatever Nate’s team is called.  He clearly tanked and then tried to masque it as something else, a strategy unworthy of glory at the fantasy throne.   Second, a boon to Boone for handling this charade well and keeping the league interesting.  
 
Herb Stomp (#1)
 
Power level: lich king.  While still dueling for the top spot with #2 and #3, Herb Stomp posted the most respectable point output of the top three teams despite having his best player on bye.  The team has an average age shy of 26, with young talent and reliable performers in key positions.  On the other hand, Cooper Kupp has been injured most of the season and underperformed in his last two games.  Herb Stomp is a threat and a legit championship contender.  If he doesn’t prevail, the future is bright with the likely #1 pick in a draft full of QB and WR talent.
 
The Legion of Bouz (#2)
 
Power level: colossal trash golem.  This team is not garbage, for now.  The Legion of Bouz has an average age of 27.  It just posted a game with less than 120 points.  CMC is getting married to former Miss USA soon and will probably settle down so his future kids with unparalleled genes can play for Stanford.  Mahomes, Waddle and DeVonta Smith are young talent that can keep this team relevant for at least a couple more years.  A win is expected next week should his opponent continue to tank.  If not for this favorable matchup and historic performance, the team could easily be ranked lower.
 
The Boonist Monks (#3)
 
Power level: shapeshifting monk master.  A series of strategic trades have made this team a contender now.  But I do mean now.  The average age is 27 and the monk master traded his soul (or, rather, picks) for instant performance mostly from older players.  Like The Legion of Bouz, this team just scored less than 120 points.   If this keeps up, he will have to shapeshift again to prevail and stay relevant.  Fortunately, the monk is up against an inconsistent opponent building for the future.  If not for this favorable matchup and historic performance, the team could easily be ranked lower.
 
Noble FT (#4)
 
Power level: Undead berserker.  Noble FT has two of the youngest and most talented running backs in Bijan Robinson and Breece Hall.  Unfortunately, those two running backs are part of sub-par teams (why does ATL draft and then under-utilize freak athletes?).  In any event, with an age shy of 26, this team has a bright future despite an immediate match up against a tough opponent in Giant Leap.
 
Giant Leap (#5)
 
Power level: Decrepit giant.  The average age here is 27.  Some of his top performers like Derrick Henry, Stefon Diggs and Keenan Allen likely have a couple years in the league before their bones and muscles become too frail for the league.  For now, though, they are still giants on the field (just not NY Giants) and could help him make the leap to a ship.  Also, did you know he has two first round draft picks?
 
General Ken-obi (#6)
 
Power level: telepathy warrior.  This team has young studs in every position, which is to be expected from the team in the league with the youngest players (23.7 years).  It was tough to place this team here with CeeDee Lamb’s recent standout games and the fresh acquisition of Saquon.  This team very well could sneak into the ship earlier than anticipated.
 
DPrince That’s Promised (#7)
 
Power level: lower zombie prince.  Tua has been a stud and D. Johnson’s reemergence is welcome relief after Justin Jefferson ended up on IR.  There are other young supporting cast members on this team that has an average age of 26.1.  He faces a tough matchup against the youngest team in the league, in General Ken-obi.
 
Kittler on the Roof (#8)
 
Power level: Adept bard.  Burrow is back to form.  This coincides nicely with JT’s recent return and his gradual claiming of more carries from Moss.  Nacua has been inconsistent of late yet is one of the pleasant surprises from this year’s stacked rookie class.  And this team is one of the youngest, with an average age of 25.4.  This team very well could have been much higher and has a nearly guaranteed win against the team that will almost certainly be our league’s Sacko.
 
BROBTIME (#9)
 
Power level: mercenary rogue.  This RB factory also has at least two strong receivers in Chase and the oft under-rated (but widely inconsistent) Gabe Davis.  The average team age is 26.6.  It’s hard to anticipate how this team will perform after its latest week when BROBTIME deliberately benched some of its best players.  If the league needs a villain, BROTIME has given it one.
 
Ghastly Grayskull Gang (#10)
 
Power level: young ghost.  This is the league’s second youngest team and recently put up 129.7 points while starting five rookies.  Stars like Amon-Ra, Swift and multiple first round picks mean the future is bright for this team. But its immediate future brings tough matchups and an uphill battle to even reach the playoffs.  Maybe next year.
 
Father Time (#11)
 
Power level: old man.  After Father Time’s initial strategy to draft studs and go for the win now seemed to implode, Father Time has turned its ancient gaze to rebuilding.  The team average age is 27.   Father Time managed to scrape a nominal win (with just 94 points) against BROBTIME, which deliberately tanked.
 
Team Chudders (#12)
 
Power level: sacko.  This team is bad.  Like super garbage, rubble, trash.  It has select quality players like Josh Allen and emerging playmakers like Gibbs and JSN.  In a puzzling move, Team Chudders traded away its first draft pick, which very well could be the first pick overall.
Top notch, Oscar! Had me cracking up to start the day. Love the format and the creativity everyone is brining to these!

CA lemon law has always been consumer friendly (e.g. consumer is entitled to attorney fees in they “prevail”, but not the other way around; availability of civil penalties of up to two times actual damages for “wilful failure” to comply with lemon law), but the recent massive year to year increase of lemon law lawsuit filings is a result of a much more aggressive LL consumer attorney bar. They are not only filing more cases but are also adding additional claims like fraud and unfair business practices that holds up resolution of the case (essentially holding the statutorily defined LL claims and its damages hostage because of the availability of punitive damages. 
Additionally, recent appellate law in the area is mostly plaintiff friendly is very impactful. For example, a recent CA Supreme Court cases found that auto manufacturers are not entitled to a monetary set off if the plaintiff sells/trades in their vehicle or receives receives insurance proceeds for an accident. This means that a plaintiff, either before or after filing a lawsuit, can sell their vehicle and still receive full restitution for their vehicle, allowing for double recovery. 
Because the deck is so stacked against the auto companies, you see a lot more repurchase (or more) offers early in cases in an attempt to keep attorney fees down. It also means a lot more cases go to trial, because auto companies offer high statutory settlement offers and if plaintiff fails to beat the offer at trial, then attorney fees are cutoff and the auto company is entitled to some costs. I’ve had 2 jury trials in last 3 months and probably will have 2-3 more this year at a minimum. That’s quite a lot considering 99% of civil cases settle before trial.
